sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Confocal microscopy in HEK293T cells: full-length MARCO-Myc showed strong colocalization with VZV gE at the cell membrane; SRCR-deleted MARCO-Myc showed markedly reduced overlap, confirming the SRCR domain (and thus the full-length tagged construct) is functional for VZV gE binding. Surface trafficking and SRCR-mediated ligand binding are preserved.
sites.rationale: MARCO is a type II transmembrane receptor (N-in, C-out); its sole extracellular terminus is the C-terminus at residue 520 (V). The 'MARCO-Myc' naming convention and the presence of Myc in both full-length and SRCR-deleted constructs (L4) together place the tag after residue 520, 455 residues from the TM boundary — well clear of the ≥3-residue constraint. L5 confirms surface display and preserved SRCR-domain function, yielding surface_and_function validation. No residue number is stated, so position_evidence is topology_derived. Full-length MARCO-Myc expressed in HEK293T cells (L4/L5, PMC13198062). The Myc tag is C-terminal: both full-length and SRCR-deleted MARCO carry the Myc tag, ruling out an internal SRCR-domain placement and placing it after the last residue of whichever construct is used; in full-length MARCO that is residue 520. MARCO is a type II single-pass TM protein with its C-terminus extracellular (residues 66–520), so the C-terminal Myc is surface-exposed.

sources.claim: Full-length MARCO-Myc and scavenger receptor cysteine-rich (SRCR) domain-lacking MARCO-Myc plasmids were previously reported [ 26 ]. pTargeT-VZV gE (a gift from Charles Grose; Addgene plasmid #60845) has been previously described [ 27 ], while pCMV3-hTLR2-HA plasmid was purchased from Sino Biological (HG10061-CY).

literature_notes: L1/L2/L3 (PMC4636388) describe a GFP-MARCO construct made with the pcDNA6.2/N-EmGFP vector, which places EmGFP at the N-terminus of the cloned insert. MARCO's N-terminus (residues 1–47) is intracellular per the topology landmarks; therefore the GFP tag faces the cytoplasm and does not qualify as an extracellular surface site. It is recorded in other_positions. L4/L5 (PMC13198062) ground the single qualifying site: a C-terminal Myc tag on full-length MARCO that is surface-displayed and functionally competent for SRCR-mediated VZV gE binding.

literature_other_positions.note: pcDNA6.2/N-EmGFP fuses EmGFP before MARCO residue 1; the MARCO N-terminus (residues 1–47) is intracellular, so this GFP tag is cytoplasmic and not a surface tag site.
